svg.title: Additive transformations translate the graph
svg.desc: Three parabolas. The solid one is the parent function, one half x squared, with its vertex at the origin. One dashed curve is the same shape lifted three units, which is the parent with three added to its output. The other dashed curve is the same shape moved two units to the RIGHT, which is the parent with minus two added to its input. A change to the output moves the graph the way the sign reads; a change to the input moves it the opposite way, so adding a negative number inside shifts right rather than left.
svg.text: f(x) + k moves it vertically; f(x + h) moves it horizontally by −h
Inside the function, the shift goes the OPPOSITE way to the sign.
